st: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Cook the onions for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, cinnamon, cardamom, cloves and dried lime and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken, salt, cumin, coriander and pepper. Brown the chicken on all sides for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, tomato paste and half the carrots. Cook for 5 minutes, then add [[4 cups]] hot water.
Cover and simmer for 25 minutes until the chicken is cooked to 165°F/74°C. Lift the chicken out and keep it warm.
Drain the soaked rice and add it to the broth with the rest of the carrots and the raisins. Taste the liquid and adjust the salt.
Bring to a boil, cover tightly, reduce the heat to very low and cook for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Meanwhile, brown the chicken under a hot broiler for 5 minutes to crisp the skin.
Fluff the rice, top with the chicken and sprinkle with the toasted almonds.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Mix the cumin, coriander, turmeric, pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt, then rub it all over the lamb with the garlic.
Put the lamb in a roasting pan with the onion, [[3 cups]] water, the cardamom, cinnamon and cloves. Cover tightly with foil.
Roast for 2.5 hours until the lamb is very tender and falls from the bone. Add a splash of water if the pan dries out.
Lift the lamb out and keep it covered and warm. Strain the cooking liquid and measure [[4.5 cups]] into a large pot, adding water if needed.
Add the drained rice, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and half the ghee. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Fluff the rice and stir in the saffron water. Cover and rest 5 minutes.
Brush the lamb with the remaining ghee and broil for 5 minutes to brown the edges.
Pile the rice on a large platter, set the lamb on top and scatter with the raisins and almonds.
Soak the cracked wheat in cold water for 1 hour, then drain.
In a large pot, put the chicken, diced onion, cinnamon, cardamom, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[8 cups]] water. Bring to a boil and skim any foam.
Simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F/74°C and is tender.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat and discard the skin and bones. Strain the broth.
Return [[6 cups]] of broth to the pot and add the drained wheat. Cook on low heat for 40 minutes, stirring often, until very soft.
Mash the wheat with a wooden spoon or potato masher until thick and creamy, adding more broth if needed. Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter, the yogurt, cumin, pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt.
Add the shredded chicken and cook for 5 minutes more.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and fry the sliced onion for 10 minutes until dark golden.
Spoon the porridge into bowls and top with the fried onion and a drizzle of the butter.

ing: white and light green parts, finely chopped
st: Mix the flour, [[1 tsp]] salt, [[2 tbsp]] oil and the warm water. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Divide into 6 balls, coat them in oil and rest for 30 minutes.
Cook the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F/71°C. Drain extra fat.
Add the onion, leeks and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the cumin, pepper and [[0.5 tsp]] salt and let it cool a little.
Stir in the parsley and the beaten eggs. The eggs will cook in the pastry.
On an oiled counter, stretch one ball of dough into a very thin square, as big as you can make it without tearing.
Put a sixth of the filling in the middle and fold in the four sides to make a sealed square package.
Heat a little oil in a wide skillet over medium heat. Fry each package for 4 minutes per side until golden and the egg is set.
Cut into squares and serve hot with lemon wedges or a yogurt dip.
Put the chicken, onion, half the cardamom and [[6 cups]] water in a large pot. Bring to a boil and skim off foam.
Add [[1 tsp]] salt, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until the chicken reaches 165°F/74°C.
Lift out the chicken and keep it warm. Strain the broth and measure [[3 cups]].
Return the broth to the pot and add the rice and the remaining cardamom. Cook on low heat for 15 minutes, stirring often.
Pour in the milk, a little at a time, stirring. Continue cooking for 15 minutes until the rice is soft and creamy like risotto.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Meanwhile, brown the chicken pieces in the remaining [[1 tbsp]] butter for 5 minutes per side to crisp the skin.
Spoon the creamy rice onto a platter and serve the chicken on top.
Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, [[2 tbsp]] oil, paprika, cumin, turmeric, cinnamon, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Add the chicken and turn to coat. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to overnight.
Heat the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the chicken in a single layer for 6 minutes per side until deeply browned and cooked to 165°F/74°C.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes, then slice it into thin strips.
Warm the pitas in a dry pan or in the oven.
Spread each pita with tahini or garlic sauce, add chicken, pickles and tomato and roll up tightly.
Toast the rolls in the pan for 1 minute per side if you like a crisp outside, then serve.

ing: whole wheat berries or pearled wheat
st: Drain the soaked wheat and rinse it well.
Put the meat, onion, cinnamon stick, cardamom and [[10 cups]] water in a large heavy pot. Bring to a boil and skim off foam.
Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 1 hour until the meat is tender and cooked through (chicken 165°F/74°C).
Lift out the meat, shred it and discard the bones. Remove the onion and whole spices.
Add the wheat to the broth with [[1 tsp]] salt. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours, stirring now and then, until the wheat is very soft.
Return the shredded meat to the pot. Beat the mixture hard with a wooden spoon or masher for 10 minutes until it turns into a thick, smooth porridge.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] butter and [[1 tsp]] salt, adding hot water if it is too stiff.
Serve in a shallow dish. Make a well in the middle, pour in the remaining [[2 tbsp]] melted butter and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Mix the flour, sugar, [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom and salt in a large bowl.
Add the melted butter, saffron milk and warm milk. Mix and knead gently until a soft smooth dough forms. Rest it for 20 minutes.
For the filling, mash the dates with [[1 tbsp]] butter, the cinnamon and the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom into a thick paste.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Take a piece of dough the size of a walnut and flatten it in your palm. Put a small ball of date paste in the middle and close the dough around it.
Roll the ball smooth and press lightly into a round cookie, or press into a cookie mold.
Bake for 18 minutes until pale golden on the bottom and set.
Cool for 10 minutes on the tray before moving them, as they are fragile when warm.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch, yeast, sugar, salt and cardamom in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and beat for 3 minutes into a thick, sticky, stretchy batter that drops slowly from a spoon.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot until doubled and bubbly.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Stir the batter once. Scoop a small spoonful with a wet spoon and push it off into the oil with another wet spoon or your hand.
Fry in small batches for 3 minutes, turning, until deep golden brown and puffed. Do not crowd the pot.
Drain the fried dumplings on a plate lined with paper towels.
Pile the hot dumplings on a plate, drizzle with the date syrup and sprinkle with the toasted sesame seeds. Serve at once.

ing: finely ground, or lightly roasted coffee
st: Bring the water to a boil in a small pot or dallah.
Add the coffee and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for 10 minutes, without stirring much, until the coffee darkens slightly and foams.
Meanwhile, put the cardamom, saffron and cloves in a thermos or serving pot.
Take the coffee off the heat and let the grounds settle for 2 minutes.
Pour the coffee through a fine strainer into the serving pot over the spices.
Let it steep for 3 minutes, then pour small amounts into tiny cups.
Serve with dates, filling cups only a third full and offering refills.
